title: Thresholded SLO Relay and Soft Circuit Bridge
author: Samir Kapoor
release_notes: Adds a thresholded SLO relay that delegates excess load to lower-cost soft circuits and introduces observability for relay decisions. Feature guarded behind runtime flag. Rolling rollout planned to 10% -> 50% -> 100% traffic. No breaking changes.
description:
Motivation: During sustained latency SLO pressure some tenants experience hard failures or abrupt degradation. This change implements a thresholded SLO relay that (1) enforces soft per-tenant delegation when local SLOs cross configured thresholds and (2) bridges requests to a lower-cost, lower-QoS "soft" circuit rather than immediately tripping a hard circuit breaker. The relay is conservative by default and is controlled by a runtime flag (runtime.slo_relay.enabled).

Design summary: The SLO relay runs inside the request router and maintains an exponentially weighted moving average (EWMA) of observed tail latency and error rate per tenant-window. When metrics cross a configured threshold (tenant_slo.window_ms and tenant_slo.error_rate_pct), the relay starts steering a configurable percentage of new requests to an attached soft circuit (soft-circuit reduces concurrency and uses a degraded model variant). The soft circuit responds with an explicit header indicating degraded path. The relay supports graceful un-winding: if the SLO metrics return below the release threshold for a cooldown period, traffic is phased back to normal.

Key characteristics: single request-level plugin with no model change, feature flag gated, tenant-configurable thresholds, hysteresis and cooldown windows to prevent flip-flopping, integrated telemetry and traces (relay.decision and relay.reason tags). The relay complements the existing circuit-breaker by deferring hard tripping until soft-circuit saturation is reached.

Implementation notes: - New module: src/runtime/slo_relay.go implements EWMA windows and routing decisions. - Soft circuit abstraction: src/runtime/soft_circuit.go encapsulates degraded model selection, reduced concurrency pools, and circuit health counters. - Router integration: router/mux.go updated to consult SloRelay.Decide(ctx, tenant) and tag routed requests. - Configuration: ops/helm/values-shedding.yaml adds flags and sane defaults used in CI tests. - Observability: metrics added (relay_decisions_total, relay_rollbacks_total, relay_duration_ms), tracing span "slo_relay.decision" and structured logs for auditability.

Testing & validation: Unit tests added for decision logic and hysteresis: tests/unit/slo_relay_test.go. Integration tests simulate tenant latency spikes and verify phased delegation and rollback: tests/integration/relay_integration_test.go. Canary run: deployed to staging and 10% of production traffic for 48 hours with synthetic spike generator. Observed behavior: relay took effect when tail p95 crossed configured threshold, soft-circuit served 18% of traffic with no client-visible errors, system CPU increased by ~2% under test.

Rollout plan: Feature is behind runtime flag runtime.slo_relay.enabled. Rollout schedule: 10% traffic for 24-48h (monitor relay_decisions_total, svc_p95 and errors), 50% for 48h, full rollout. Abort criteria: sustained increase in client 5xx > 0.5 percentage points or p95 regression > 15% compared to baseline.

Migration and compatibility: No schema or API changes. Soft circuit adds a response header X-Redwood-Degraded: true when used. Customers may opt out by tenant config (tenant.slo_relay.mode=off).

Risks & mitigations: - Risk of double-routing causing increased cost: mitigated by conservative default delegation percent (10%) and global budget cap. - Risk of oscillation: mitigated by hysteresis windows and exponential cooldown. - Observability blind spots: added metrics and a dashboard to surface relay activity and tenant-level outcomes.

Follow-ups: - ENG-3003: add automated rollout canary gating to Console. - ENG-2240: enable per-model degradation profiles for better quality tuning.

References: Linear ENG-2145, manual runbook updates in docs/ops/graceful-relay.md.
